seo_title: PM Surya Ghar Subsidy Ads: How Installers Advertise It Right
description: How solar installers can use the PM Surya Ghar subsidy in ads and landing pages: honest wording, claims to avoid, platform rules and pages that convert.
headline: PM Surya Ghar subsidy ads: how solar installers can use the subsidy without misleading anyone
card_text: How to put the rooftop solar subsidy into Meta ads, Google ads and landing pages honestly: current figures, risky claims to avoid, safer wording and a page structure that turns subsidy interest into site visits.
intro:
PM Surya Ghar subsidy ads are everywhere in Indian rooftop solar right now, and for good reason. The scheme gives homeowners a clear reason to act, and "How much subsidy will I get?" is usually the first question on every enquiry call. Used well, the subsidy lowers your cost per lead and shortens the sales cycle.

Used badly, it brings the wrong leads and damages trust. Ads that promise "free solar", borrow government logos or hide the real price attract people who drop off once they hear the actual cost, and they can get your ads rejected. This guide shows solar installers and EPCs how to use the subsidy in ads and landing pages honestly, with wording you can adapt, claims to avoid and a page structure that turns subsidy interest into site visits.

sections.h2: Why the subsidy is your strongest hook and your biggest risk
sections.html:
Most homeowners don't wake up thinking about solar panels. They do think about their electricity bill, and a government-backed subsidy turns a vague idea into a decision with a clear, money-saving benefit. That's why a subsidy message often gets more attention than a generic "go solar" ad.

The risk comes from the same place. Because the scheme is called Muft Bijli Yojana, many people believe the panels themselves are free. If your ad plays on that confusion, you'll attract unhappy leads, and serious buyers will scroll past because the offer looks too good to be true.

The goal is simple: make the subsidy the reason to enquire, and make your company the reason to trust.

sections.h2: What the scheme offers right now
sections.html:
Before you write a single headline, get the facts right. These are the central figures for residential rooftop solar under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana at the time of writing. They can change, so check pmsuryaghar.gov.in and your DISCOM before every campaign.

ItemCurrent position
Central subsidy, 1 kW₹30,000
Central subsidy, 2 kW₹60,000
Central subsidy, 3 kW and above₹78,000 (capped)
Housing societies and RWAs (common areas)₹18,000 per kW, within the scheme's capacity limit
Who pays itCredited to the homeowner's bank account after commissioning, not deducted by the installer
Who can installVendors registered on the national portal, using approved (ALMM-listed) modules
State top-upsSome states add their own support; amounts differ and change
Bank loansConcessional loans through participating banks; check current rates and limits

Two points matter for marketing. The subsidy goes to the customer, not to you, so quotes should show the full price and expected subsidy separately. And only registered vendors can deliver a subsidised installation: if you're registered, show it; if not, don't advertise the subsidy as something you can deliver.

sections.h2: Claims to avoid in PM Surya Ghar subsidy ads
sections.html:
Most problems come from a handful of phrases. Here is what to drop and what to say instead.

Risky claimWhy it's a problemSafer wording
"Free solar panels for your home"The panels are not free; the subsidy covers part of the cost"Get up to ₹78,000 central subsidy on rooftop solar"
"Zero electricity bill guaranteed"Savings depend on usage, roof, location and tariff"Cut your electricity bill with rooftop solar"
"Government solar scheme, apply here"Implies you are the government or the official portal"We're a registered vendor. We help you apply on the official portal."
"Subsidy approved in 7 days"Timelines depend on the DISCOM and the portal, not on you"We handle the paperwork and keep you updated at every step"
"Last few days to claim the subsidy!"False urgency; erodes trust when it isn't true"Subsidy amounts can change. Check your eligibility today."
"3 kW solar for just ₹X" (net price only)Hides the full cost the customer pays upfront"3 kW system from ₹X before subsidy; up to ₹78,000 back after commissioning"

Also avoid the national emblem, ministry logos, the Prime Minister's photo and any design that copies the official portal. You are a private company helping people use a public scheme, and your ads should look like it.

sections.h2: Subsidy-led ad copy that stays honest
sections.html:
Honest ads don't have to be dull. Lead with a local, specific benefit and use the subsidy as the reason to act now. Patterns worth testing:

  1. The bill angle: "Paying ₹4,000+ a month for electricity in Dwarka? A 3 kW rooftop system could cut that sharply, and you may be eligible for up to ₹78,000 central subsidy."
  2. The paperwork angle: "Confused by the PM Surya Ghar portal? As a registered vendor, we handle the application, DISCOM approval and net meter for you."
  3. The local proof angle: a 20-second video of a real installation in your city, with the caption "Installed last week in Rohini. Subsidy application filed on the official portal."
  4. The question angle for Google Search: headlines such as "Rooftop solar subsidy help", "Registered PM Surya Ghar vendor" and "Free site survey in Gurugram", with a description that mentions the full price range.

In Meta lead forms, add one qualifying question about the monthly bill and one about property ownership. Our step-by-step guide to Facebook ads for solar installers covers the full form setup, and our list of solar ad creative ideas has more video and image formats to test.

sections.h2: Platform rules on Meta and Google
sections.html:
Both platforms review ads for misleading claims, and subsidy ads get extra attention because scammers use the same words. Keep your account healthy:

  • Make it clear who you are. Your business name should appear in the ad and on the landing page. Don't name the page or ad account in a way that sounds like a government department.
  • Match the ad to the page. If the ad mentions ₹78,000, the landing page should explain the same figure and how it is paid.
  • Never collect what the portal collects. Don't ask for Aadhaar numbers, bank details or OTPs in a lead form. A name, phone number, city and bill range are enough.
  • Keep claims checkable. Savings examples should say they are estimates and depend on usage and location.
  • Watch for policy updates. Meta and Google change their ad policies often, including rules on government-related services. Check the current policies before you launch, and fix any rejected ad by changing the claim, not by rewording it to slip past review.

If you run Google Search for subsidy keywords, add negatives such as "apply online", "status", "login" and "form". People typing those want the official portal, not an installer, and the clicks are expensive. Our Google Ads team adds these to every solar account.

sections.h2: Building a subsidy landing page that converts
sections.html:
The landing page does the heavy lifting. Someone who clicked a subsidy ad wants three answers fast: how much, am I eligible and can I trust you. Structure the page in this order:

  1. Headline: "Rooftop solar with up to ₹78,000 central subsidy, installed by a registered vendor in [city]".
  2. The real numbers: a simple table showing system size, typical price before subsidy, central subsidy and any state support, with a note that prices depend on the roof and equipment.
  3. Proof you are registered: tell visitors they can check your name on the official vendor list themselves, and show your company details clearly.
  4. The process in plain steps: site survey, portal application, DISCOM approval, installation, net meter, inspection, subsidy credited to your account.
  5. Local installations: photos and short videos of real rooftops in your area, plus genuine Google reviews.
  6. A short form or WhatsApp button: name, phone, area and monthly bill range. Nothing more.
  7. FAQs: who gets the money, how long it usually takes, what happens if the application is rejected, and whether renters can apply.
  8. A one-line disclaimer: "Subsidy amounts and eligibility are set by the government and may change. We are a private company and a registered vendor under the scheme."

The disclaimer won't scare serious buyers off; it shows you know the rules.

sections.h2: Turning subsidy enquiries into site visits
sections.html:
Subsidy leads need fast, clear follow-up. Call within ten minutes during working hours. If they don't answer, send a WhatsApp message that explains the subsidy in two lines and offers a free site survey slot.

On the first call, answer the subsidy question honestly, then move to the roof, the bill and the timeline. Explain that the subsidy is credited to their own bank account after commissioning, that you will never ask for an OTP and that they can verify you on the official portal. With so many "free solar" scams going around, that reassurance is often what wins the survey.

When the system is installed and the subsidy lands, ask for a Google review that mentions it. A local review saying "they handled the whole subsidy process" is worth more than any ad headline. Our guide to solar lead generation in India has a simple scoring system for deciding which subsidy enquiries deserve a visit first.

This is how we run subsidy campaigns for the 30+ solar EPCs and manufacturers we work with, where well-run rooftop campaigns deliver qualified enquiries at ₹60–80 each. faqs: Can solar installers mention the PM Surya Ghar subsidy in ads?

Yes. Registered vendors can mention the subsidy as long as the figures are current and accurate, the ad makes clear you are a private company, and you don't promise free solar, guaranteed approval or fixed timelines. Check pmsuryaghar.gov.in before each campaign.
How much is the PM Surya Ghar subsidy for a 3 kW system?

At the time of writing, central assistance is ₹78,000 for residential systems of 3 kW and above, ₹60,000 for 2 kW and ₹30,000 for 1 kW. Some states add their own support. Amounts can change, so confirm on the official portal.
Is it legal to use the government logo in solar ads?

Avoid it. Using the national emblem, ministry logos, the Prime Minister's photo or a design that copies the official portal can mislead people into thinking you are the government, and ad platforms may reject such ads. Use your own brand and say you are a registered vendor.
Does the installer get the PM Surya Ghar subsidy?
No. The central subsidy is credited to the homeowner's bank account after the system is commissioned and inspected. Installers should quote the full price and show the expected subsidy separately.
Why are my solar subsidy ads getting rejected?

Common reasons are claims like free solar or zero bills, wording that implies you are a government body, and landing pages that don't match the ad. Fix the claim itself, make your company name clear and check the platform's current ad policies.
